questions.text: Which of the following correctly describes the magnetic field near a long straight wire carrying current?

options.text: Straight lines perpendicular to the wire
Straight lines parallel to the wire
Radial lines originating from the wire
Concentric circles centred on the wire

key_points: Magnetic field lines around a straight current-carrying conductor are concentric circles in a plane perpendicular to the wire
rubric.expected_answer: (d) Concentric circles centred on the wire

questions.text: In the Right-Hand Thumb Rule for a straight current-carrying conductor, the curled fingers of the right hand represent the direction of:

key_points: Thumb points in direction of current; curled fingers show direction of magnetic field lines
rubric.expected_answer: (b) Magnetic field around the conductor

questions.text: The force experienced by a current-carrying conductor placed in a magnetic field is LARGEST when:

options.text: The conductor is parallel to the magnetic field
The conductor makes a 45° angle with the magnetic field
The conductor is perpendicular to the magnetic field
The conductor is at 30° to the magnetic field

key_points: Force F = BIL sinθ; maximum when θ = 90°, i.e. conductor perpendicular to B
rubric.expected_answer: (c) The conductor is perpendicular to the magnetic field

questions.text: At the time of short circuit, the current in the circuit:

key_points: In a short circuit the resistance drops to near zero; by Ohm's law I = V/R, current surges to a very large value
rubric.expected_answer: (c) Increases heavily

questions.text: The magnetic field inside a long straight solenoid carrying current is:

options.text: Decreasing as we move towards its end
Increasing as we move towards its end

key_points: Inside a solenoid the field lines are parallel and equally spaced, indicating a uniform magnetic field
rubric.expected_answer: (d) The same at all points (uniform)

questions.text: A device that works on the principle of the force experienced by a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field is:

key_points: Electric motor converts electrical energy to mechanical energy using the force on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field
rubric.expected_answer: (c) Electric motor

questions.text: Two magnetic field lines can never intersect each other because:

options.text: Field lines always travel in straight paths
At any given point the magnetic field has a unique direction, so two lines meeting would imply two directions
Field lines can only originate from the north pole

key_points: At any point in space the magnetic field has one definite direction; if two field lines crossed, a compass needle placed there would point in two directions simultaneously — which is physically impossible
rubric.expected_answer: (b) At any given point the magnetic field has a unique direction, so two lines meeting would imply two directions

questions.text: A circular coil has 20 turns and carries the same current as a single-turn circular coil of the same radius. The magnetic field at the centre of the 20-turn coil compared to the single-turn coil is:

key_points: The magnetic field at the centre of a circular coil is directly proportional to the number of turns; B ∝ n
rubric.expected_answer: (c) 20 times as large

questions.text: In domestic electric circuits, the wire with GREEN insulation is the:

key_points: Live = red insulation; Neutral = black insulation; Earth = green insulation
rubric.expected_answer: (c) Earth wire

questions.text: List THREE properties of magnetic field lines.

key_points: Field lines emerge from the north pole and enter the south pole outside the magnet; they form closed loops inside
The tangent to a field line at any point gives the direction of the magnetic field at that point
Two magnetic field lines never intersect each other
Where field lines are closer (crowded) the magnetic field is stronger; where they are farther apart the field is weaker
rubric.expected_answer: Any three from: (1) They form closed continuous loops from N to S outside and S to N inside the magnet. (2) The tangent at any point on a field line gives the direction of B at that point. (3) Two field lines never cross each other. (4) Closer field lines indicate a stronger field.

questions.text: State the Right-Hand Thumb Rule used to determine the direction of the magnetic field around a straight current-carrying conductor.

key_points: Hold the conductor in the right hand such that the thumb points in the direction of current flow
The curled (wrapped) fingers indicate the direction of the magnetic field around the conductor
rubric.expected_answer: Imagine holding the current-carrying conductor in the right hand so that the thumb points in the direction of the current. Then the fingers wrapped around the conductor give the direction of the magnetic field lines around it.

questions.text: State Fleming's Left-Hand Rule.

key_points: Stretch the forefinger, middle finger, and thumb of the left hand mutually perpendicular to each other
Forefinger → direction of magnetic field (B)
Middle finger → direction of current (I)
Thumb → direction of force/motion on the conductor
rubric.expected_answer: Stretch the forefinger, middle finger, and thumb of the left hand so that they are mutually perpendicular. If the forefinger points in the direction of the magnetic field and the middle finger points in the direction of the current, then the thumb gives the direction of the force (motion) on the conductor.

questions.text: What is the function of an earth wire in domestic electric circuits? Why is it necessary to earth metallic appliances?

key_points: Earth wire provides a low-resistance conducting path to the ground for any leakage current
If a live wire accidentally touches the metallic casing of an appliance, the current is safely discharged to earth, preventing electric shock to the user
rubric.expected_answer: The earth wire connects the metallic body of an appliance directly to the earth (ground). Its function is to provide a low-resistance path so that any leakage current due to a fault flows harmlessly to the earth. This prevents the metallic casing from becoming live and protects the user from electric shock.

questions.text: Why does a compass needle get deflected when brought near a bar magnet?

key_points: A bar magnet has a magnetic field around it
The compass needle is itself a small magnet; the magnetic force exerted by the bar magnet on the needle causes it to align along the local field direction, making it deflect
rubric.expected_answer: A bar magnet produces a magnetic field in the region surrounding it. A compass needle is a small freely pivoted magnet. When brought near the bar magnet, the magnetic force exerted by the bar magnet's field acts on the poles of the compass needle, causing it to rotate and align along the direction of the local magnetic field — hence it gets deflected.

questions.text: How does the magnetic field produced by a straight current-carrying conductor change with (i) increasing distance from the conductor and (ii) increasing magnitude of current?

key_points: (i) The magnetic field decreases as distance from the conductor increases (B ∝ 1/r)
(ii) The magnetic field increases as the current in the conductor increases (B ∝ I)
rubric.expected_answer: (i) The magnetic field strength decreases as the distance from the conductor increases — the field lines spread out and become less dense farther away. (ii) The magnetic field strength increases as the current through the conductor increases — a larger current produces a stronger field.

questions.text: Imagine you are sitting in a chamber with your back to one wall. An electron beam moving horizontally from the back wall towards the front wall is deflected to your right side by a strong magnetic field. What is the direction of the magnetic field?

key_points: Electrons move from back to front, so conventional current direction is from front to back (opposite to electron motion)
Force on the beam is towards the right (given)
Using Fleming's Left-Hand Rule: forefinger (B) pointing downward, middle finger (current: front→back), thumb (force: rightward) — B is vertically downward
rubric.expected_answer: The electron beam moves from back to front, so the conventional current direction is from front to back. The force is directed to the right. Applying Fleming's Left-Hand Rule (middle finger = current direction front-to-back; thumb = force to the right), the forefinger (direction of B) points vertically downward. Therefore, the magnetic field is directed vertically downward.

questions.text: When does an electric short circuit occur? Name TWO safety devices used in domestic electric circuits to prevent damage from excessive current.

key_points: Short circuit occurs when the live wire and the neutral wire come into direct contact, causing resistance to drop to nearly zero and current to surge
Safety devices: (1) Electric fuse (2) Miniature Circuit Breaker (MCB)
rubric.expected_answer: A short circuit occurs when the live wire and the neutral wire come into direct contact (e.g., due to damaged insulation). The resistance drops to nearly zero, causing current to increase suddenly to a very high value. Two safety devices: (1) Electric fuse — melts and breaks the circuit when current exceeds its rated value. (2) MCB (Miniature Circuit Breaker) — automatically trips the circuit on overload or short circuit.

questions.text: How is the magnetic field produced by a current-carrying solenoid similar to that of a bar magnet? Explain with reference to the magnetic field pattern.

key_points: The magnetic field lines of a solenoid outside it closely resemble those of a bar magnet — they emerge from one end (N-pole) and enter the other end (S-pole)
Inside the solenoid the field is uniform (parallel lines) just as inside a bar magnet
One end of the solenoid acts as a north pole (field lines emerge) and the other as a south pole (field lines enter)
rubric.expected_answer: A current-carrying solenoid produces a magnetic field pattern very similar to a bar magnet: (1) Outside — the field lines emerge from one end (acting as N-pole) and curve around to re-enter the other end (acting as S-pole), identical to a bar magnet's external field. (2) Inside — the field lines are parallel and equally spaced, indicating a strong, uniform magnetic field, analogous to the uniform field inside a bar magnet. (3) The polarity (N or S) of each end depends on the direction of current flow.

questions.text: In an experiment, a current-carrying rod AB placed between the poles of a horseshoe magnet is displaced towards the left. Predict how the displacement of rod AB will be affected if: (i) current in AB is increased, (ii) a stronger horseshoe magnet is used, (iii) the direction of current through AB is reversed.

key_points: (i) Displacement increases — greater current → greater force on the conductor
(ii) Displacement increases — stronger magnet → stronger field → greater force
(iii) Displacement reverses direction (rod moves to the right) — reversing current reverses the direction of force
rubric.expected_answer: (i) The displacement (and force) increases because force is directly proportional to current (F ∝ I). (ii) The displacement increases because force is proportional to the strength of the magnetic field (F ∝ B). (iii) The displacement reverses — the rod now moves to the right — because reversing the current reverses the direction of the force (Fleming's LHR).

questions.text: State the rule used to determine the direction of current induced in a coil due to its rotation in a magnetic field. How is this rule applied?

key_points: Fleming's Right-Hand Rule is used
Stretch the thumb, forefinger, and middle finger of the right hand mutually perpendicular
Forefinger → direction of magnetic field; Thumb → direction of motion of conductor; Middle finger → direction of induced current
rubric.expected_answer: Fleming's Right-Hand Rule: Stretch the thumb, forefinger, and middle finger of the right hand so they are mutually perpendicular. If the forefinger points in the direction of the magnetic field and the thumb points in the direction of motion of the conductor, then the middle finger points in the direction of the induced current.

questions.text: A current through a horizontal power line flows in the east-to-west direction. What is the direction of the magnetic field at a point (i) directly below the wire and (ii) directly above the wire?

key_points: Current flows east to west; apply Right-Hand Thumb Rule
At a point directly below the wire: magnetic field is directed from south to north (towards north)
At a point directly above the wire: magnetic field is directed from north to south (towards south)
rubric.expected_answer: Current is directed east to west. By the Right-Hand Thumb Rule (thumb east→west, fingers curl): (i) At a point directly below the wire — the field is directed from south to north (i.e., towards north). (ii) At a point directly above the wire — the field is directed from north to south (i.e., towards south). The field circles the wire; at the bottom it goes northward and at the top it goes southward.

questions.text: List TWO methods by which a magnetic field can be produced.

key_points: (1) By passing an electric current through a conductor (Oersted's discovery)
(2) By using a permanent bar magnet
rubric.expected_answer: (1) A magnetic field is produced around a current-carrying conductor when current flows through it. (2) A permanent bar magnet produces a magnetic field in the region surrounding it.

questions.text: A positively charged alpha-particle is projected towards the west and is deflected towards the north by a magnetic field. What is the direction of the magnetic field? Justify your answer using Fleming's rule.

key_points: Alpha particle is positively charged and moves west → conventional current direction is west (same as motion for positive charge)
Force is towards north
Using Fleming's LHR: middle finger (current) → west; thumb (force) → north; forefinger (B) → vertically upward
rubric.expected_answer: The alpha particle is positive and moves west, so the conventional current direction is westward. The magnetic force on it is northward. Applying Fleming's Left-Hand Rule: middle finger = west (current), thumb = north (force) — the forefinger must point vertically upward. Therefore the magnetic field is directed vertically upward.

questions.text: An electric oven of 2 kW power rating is operated in a domestic electric circuit (220 V) that has a current rating of 5 A. Calculate the current drawn by the oven. Will the fuse of 5 A rating blow? Justify your answer.

key_points: Current = Power / Voltage = 2000 W / 220 V ≈ 9.09 A
This current (9.09 A) exceeds the fuse rating of 5 A
Therefore the fuse will blow / melt, disconnecting the circuit
rubric.expected_answer: I = P/V = 2000/220 ≈ 9.09 A. Since 9.09 A > 5 A (fuse rating), the fuse will blow to protect the circuit.

questions.text: A circular coil consists of 15 turns. The magnetic field at its centre due to a single turn carrying the same current is B₀. What is the total magnetic field at the centre of the 15-turn coil?

key_points: Magnetic field at the centre of a circular coil is proportional to the number of turns: B = n × B₀
For n = 15: B = 15B₀
rubric.expected_answer: B = 15 × B₀ = 15B₀

questions.text: A room heater rated 1500 W is connected to a 220 V domestic supply. (i) Calculate the current drawn by the heater. (ii) Will a 5 A fuse be sufficient, or is a 10 A fuse needed? Justify.

key_points: 6.82 A > 5 A, so a 5 A fuse will blow
A 10 A fuse is needed (rated above the operating current with a safety margin)
rubric.expected_answer: (i) I = 1500/220 ≈ 6.82 A. (ii) A 5 A fuse is insufficient (6.82 A > 5 A and it would blow during normal operation). A 10 A fuse is needed.

questions.text: With the help of a labeled diagram, explain the magnetic field pattern due to a current flowing through a solenoid. How does a current-carrying solenoid behave like a bar magnet?

key_points: A solenoid is a long cylindrical coil of insulated copper wire; when current flows, each turn contributes to the magnetic field
Inside the solenoid: field is uniform — parallel, equally spaced field lines along the axis
Outside the solenoid: field lines form closed loops from one end to the other, resembling a bar magnet
One end becomes N-pole (field lines emerge) and the other S-pole (field lines enter) depending on current direction
Diagram must show: solenoid coil, current direction, field lines inside (parallel) and outside (looping), N and S poles labeled
rubric.expected_answer: A solenoid consists of many turns of insulated wire wound in a cylindrical form. On passing current: (1) Each turn produces a small magnetic field; these add up to produce a strong, uniform field along the axis inside the solenoid. (2) The field lines inside are parallel straight lines, indicating uniform field. (3) Outside, the field lines emerge from one end and enter the other, exactly like a bar magnet. (4) The end from which lines emerge is the N-pole; the end into which they enter is the S-pole. Thus a current-carrying solenoid acts as a bar magnet.
diagram_checklist: Solenoid coil drawn with multiple turns

questions.text: Explain the force experienced by a current-carrying conductor placed in a magnetic field. State and explain Fleming's Left-Hand Rule with a diagram. Why is the force maximum when the current is perpendicular to the magnetic field?

key_points: A current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field experiences a mechanical force (Ampere's force)
The force is perpendicular to both the current direction and the magnetic field direction
Fleming's LHR: forefinger = B direction, middle finger = I direction, thumb = force direction (all mutually perpendicular)
F = BIL sinθ; when θ = 90° (current ⊥ B), sinθ = 1 → force is maximum
When current is parallel to B (θ = 0°), force = 0
rubric.expected_answer: A current-carrying conductor in an external magnetic field experiences a force due to the interaction of the conductor's own magnetic field with the external field. The direction is given by Fleming's LHR: hold the left hand with forefinger (B), middle finger (I), and thumb (Force) mutually perpendicular — the thumb shows the direction of force. The magnitude is F = BIL sinθ. When θ = 90° (current ⊥ B), sinθ = 1 and force is maximum. When θ = 0° (current ∥ B), force is zero.
diagram_checklist: Fleming's LHR hand sketch or description

questions.text: What is a magnetic field? Draw the magnetic field lines around a bar magnet. List FOUR properties of magnetic field lines.

key_points: Magnetic field: the region around a magnet where a magnetic force is experienced; represented by field lines
Diagram: closed loops from N to S outside the magnet, S to N inside; arrows showing direction
Property 1: Field lines emerge from N-pole and enter S-pole (outside)
Property 2: They form closed continuous loops
Property 3: Two field lines never intersect
Property 4: Closer/denser lines indicate stronger field; sparser lines indicate weaker field
rubric.expected_answer: Magnetic field is the region around a magnet where a magnetic force can be detected. It is represented by magnetic field lines. Diagram: field lines emerge from N, curve around, and re-enter at S outside the magnet; they continue inside from S to N forming closed loops. Four properties: (1) Outside the magnet, lines go from N to S; inside from S to N (closed loops). (2) The tangent at any point gives the direction of B. (3) Two field lines never intersect. (4) Denser lines = stronger field; sparse lines = weaker field.
diagram_checklist: Bar magnet labeled N and S
Arrows on lines showing N→S direction outside

questions.text:
Assertion (A): Two magnetic field lines never intersect each other.
Reason (R): If two field lines were to intersect, it would imply that the magnetic field has two different directions at the point of intersection, which is physically impossible.

Choose the correct option:
(a) Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
(b) Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
(c) A is true but R is false.
(d) A is false but R is true.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

key_points: Both A and R are true; R correctly explains A — intersection implies two directions of B at one point
rubric.expected_answer: (a) Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.text:
Assertion (A): Electric fuse is an important safety device used in domestic circuits.
Reason (R): Fuse wire is made of a material with high resistance and low melting point, so it melts and breaks the circuit when current exceeds the rated value.

Choose the correct option:
(a) Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
(b) Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
(c) A is true but R is false.
(d) A is false but R is true.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

key_points: Both A and R are true; R correctly explains the working principle of a fuse
rubric.expected_answer: (a) Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.text: Draw the magnetic field lines around a bar magnet. Label the north pole, south pole, and indicate the direction of the field lines. Show at least four field lines and indicate where the field is strongest.

key_points: Bar magnet drawn and labeled N, S
At least 4 field lines drawn as closed loops
Arrows indicating direction from N to S outside
Lines denser near poles (stronger field indicated)
rubric.expected_answer: A bar magnet with N on left, S on right; smooth curved field lines emerging from N, curving around in space, and entering S; arrows on lines; lines bunched close together near poles showing strong field, spread out farther away showing weaker field.

questions.text: Draw a neat diagram showing the magnetic field pattern around a current-carrying solenoid. On the diagram, mark: (i) the direction of current in the wires, (ii) the N-pole end, (iii) the S-pole end, and (iv) the region where the magnetic field is uniform.

key_points: Solenoid shape drawn correctly
Current direction marked on turns
Parallel field lines inside (uniform field region labeled)
Curved field lines outside looping from N to S
N and S poles correctly identified at ends
rubric.expected_answer: Solenoid with multiple turns; current shown going in (×) on one side and out (•) on the other; parallel straight field lines inside labeled 'uniform field'; curved closed field lines outside; left end labeled N-pole and right end S-pole (or vice versa, consistent with current direction).

questions.text: Draw a labeled diagram of a simple electric motor. The diagram must include and label: the armature coil (ABCD), the permanent magnet (N and S poles), the split-ring commutator, the carbon brushes (X and Y), the battery, and indicate the direction of rotation of the coil.

key_points: Rectangular coil ABCD placed between magnetic poles
Split-ring commutator attached to coil ends
Carbon brushes (X and Y) in contact with commutator
Battery connected through brushes
All six components labeled
Rotation direction indicated
rubric.expected_answer: Labeled diagram showing: rectangular coil ABCD between N and S poles of permanent magnet; two half-rings (split-ring commutator) attached to ends A and D of coil; two carbon brushes X and Y pressing on commutator; battery connected to brushes; arrow showing direction of rotation of coil.
diagram_checklist: Magnet poles N and S labeled
Carbon brushes X and Y labeled

questions.text: A bar magnet is cut into two equal halves perpendicular to its length. Each half:

options.text: Becomes an independent complete magnet with both N and S poles

key_points: A magnet cannot be isolated into monopoles; each half becomes a complete magnet with both N and S poles
rubric.expected_answer: (a) Becomes an independent complete magnet with both N and S poles

questions.text: In a diagram of magnetic field lines, the lines are drawn closer together at a certain region. This indicates that:

options.text: The magnetic field is weaker there
The magnetic field is stronger there
The field lines are about to intersect
There is no magnetic force in that region

key_points: Denser (closer) field lines represent a stronger magnetic field
rubric.expected_answer: (b) The magnetic field is stronger there

questions.text: If the current through a long straight conductor is doubled, the magnetic field at a fixed distance from the conductor:

key_points: B ∝ I for a straight conductor; doubling I doubles B
rubric.expected_answer: (c) Doubles

questions.text: In the Right-Hand Thumb Rule, the thumb of the right hand points in the direction of:

key_points: Thumb = current direction; curled fingers = magnetic field direction
rubric.expected_answer: (b) Current flow

questions.text: A current-carrying conductor is placed parallel to a uniform magnetic field. The force experienced by the conductor is:

key_points: F = BIL sinθ; when conductor is parallel to B, θ = 0°, sin0° = 0, so force = 0
rubric.expected_answer: (c) Zero

questions.text: In Fleming's Left-Hand Rule, the middle finger of the left hand points in the direction of:

key_points: Forefinger = B; Middle finger = current; Thumb = force
rubric.expected_answer: (c) Direction of current

questions.text: In a household electric circuit, all appliances are connected in:

key_points: Domestic appliances are in parallel so each operates at the same 220 V and can be switched independently
rubric.expected_answer: (b) Parallel

questions.text: The potential difference between the live wire and the neutral wire in an Indian domestic electric supply is:

key_points: In India, domestic AC supply is 220 V at 50 Hz

questions.text: A proton moves in a direction parallel to a magnetic field. The force on the proton due to the magnetic field is:

key_points: F = qvB sinθ; when motion is parallel to B, θ = 0°, F = 0
rubric.expected_answer: (c) Zero

questions.text: Which of the following correctly describes how the magnetic field at the centre of a circular current-carrying loop changes when the radius is halved (current kept constant)?

key_points: B ∝ I/r; if r is halved, B doubles (with I constant)
rubric.expected_answer: (b) The field doubles

questions.text: Which of the following statements about AC and DC generators is CORRECT?

options.text: AC generator uses a split-ring commutator; DC generator uses slip rings
AC generator uses slip rings; DC generator uses a split-ring commutator

key_points: AC generator → slip rings (output alternates); DC generator → split-ring commutator (output is unidirectional)
rubric.expected_answer: (b) AC generator uses slip rings; DC generator uses a split-ring commutator

questions.text: State any FOUR properties of magnetic field lines.

key_points: 1. Field lines are closed continuous curves — outside the magnet from N to S; inside from S to N
2. The tangent at any point on a field line gives the direction of B at that point
3. Two field lines never intersect each other
4. Where lines are close together (dense) the field is strong; where they are far apart the field is weak
rubric.expected_answer: Any four: (1) Closed loops from N to S outside, S to N inside. (2) Tangent at any point = direction of B. (3) Never intersect. (4) Denser lines = stronger field.

questions.text: What is a solenoid? Explain how it can be used as an electromagnet.

key_points: A solenoid is a long cylindrical coil of insulated copper wire wound in a helix
When current flows, it produces a strong magnetic field inside
Inserting a soft iron core greatly enhances the field — forming a powerful electromagnet
rubric.expected_answer: A solenoid is a coil of insulated copper wire wound in the form of a long cylinder. When current passes through it, it produces a magnetic field similar to a bar magnet. To use it as an electromagnet, a soft iron rod is inserted as the core — the iron rod gets strongly magnetised, greatly increasing the magnetic field. The magnetism disappears when the current is switched off.

questions.text: What is electromagnetic induction? State ONE practical application of electromagnetic induction.

key_points: Electromagnetic induction: the phenomenon of producing an electric current in a conductor/coil by changing the magnetic field linked with it
Practical application: electric generator (converts mechanical energy into electrical energy)
rubric.expected_answer: Electromagnetic induction is the process of generating an electric current in a circuit by a changing magnetic field passing through it. One practical application is the electric generator, which uses electromagnetic induction to convert mechanical energy (rotation of a coil in a magnetic field) into electrical energy.

questions.text: Differentiate between an electric fuse and an MCB (Miniature Circuit Breaker) as safety devices in domestic circuits.

key_points: Fuse: wire melts (destroyed) when excess current flows; must be replaced after use; works on Joule heating
MCB: automatically trips (switches off) the circuit on overload; can be reset (reused) by flipping a switch
rubric.expected_answer: Electric fuse: the fuse wire melts when current exceeds the rated value, permanently breaking the circuit; must be replaced after blowing. MCB: automatically switches off when excess current flows; can be reset by pushing a button/switch after the fault is fixed — it is reusable.

questions.text: How is the direction of a magnetic field at a point determined using a compass needle?

key_points: A compass needle is placed at the point of interest
The needle aligns along the local magnetic field; the direction pointed by the north pole of the needle gives the direction of the magnetic field at that point
rubric.expected_answer: A small compass needle is placed at the point where the magnetic field direction is to be found. The needle aligns itself along the magnetic field. The direction pointed by the north pole of the compass needle indicates the direction of the magnetic field at that point.

questions.text: State any TWO differences between a bar magnet and an electromagnet.

key_points: Bar magnet: permanent magnet; magnetism cannot be switched off or varied
Electromagnet: temporary magnet; requires electric current; magnetism can be switched on/off and its strength can be varied by changing current or number of turns
rubric.expected_answer: (1) A bar magnet is a permanent magnet; an electromagnet is temporary and works only when current flows. (2) The strength of a bar magnet is fixed; the strength of an electromagnet can be increased or decreased by changing the current or number of turns. (Bonus: polarity of an electromagnet can be reversed by reversing the current.)

questions.text: Name the device that converts mechanical energy into electrical energy. State the principle on which it works.

key_points: Device: Electric Generator
Principle: Electromagnetic induction — when a coil rotates in a magnetic field, a changing flux induces an EMF/current in the coil
rubric.expected_answer: Device: Electric Generator. Principle: It works on electromagnetic induction. When a coil is rotated in a magnetic field (or a magnetic field is varied around a coil), the magnetic flux through the coil changes, which induces an electromotive force (EMF) and hence an electric current in the circuit.

questions.text: Why should the metallic casing of an electric iron be connected to the earth wire?

key_points: If the live wire accidentally touches the metallic casing of the electric iron, the casing becomes live
Earth wire provides a low-resistance path so the fault current flows safely to ground, preventing electric shock to the user
rubric.expected_answer: If a fault develops and the live wire touches the metal casing of the electric iron, the casing becomes live and anyone touching it would receive a severe electric shock. By connecting the casing to the earth wire, any stray current flows through the low-resistance earth wire to the ground rather than through the user's body, thereby preventing electric shock.

questions.text: Why is it physically impossible for two magnetic field lines to cross each other?

key_points: The tangent to a field line at any point gives the direction of the magnetic field at that point
At any given point the magnetic field can have only one direction
If two lines crossed, there would be two tangents at the crossing point, implying two different field directions — which is physically impossible
rubric.expected_answer: The tangent to a magnetic field line at any point gives the direction of the field at that point. At any point in space, the magnetic field has exactly one direction. If two field lines were to intersect at a point, there would be two different tangents (two different directions) at that point — which is physically impossible for a field that has a unique direction at every point.

questions.text: What happens to the magnetic field inside a solenoid when the number of turns per unit length is increased, keeping the current constant?

key_points: The magnetic field inside a solenoid is proportional to the number of turns per unit length (n)
Increasing n increases the field strength
rubric.expected_answer: The magnetic field inside a solenoid is directly proportional to the number of turns per unit length (B ∝ nI). If the number of turns is increased while current is kept constant, the magnetic field inside increases proportionally — each additional turn contributes to the total field.

questions.text: In an experiment, a current-carrying rod placed between magnet poles is displaced. Explain why the displacement increases when a stronger magnet is used.

key_points: The force on a current-carrying conductor is F = BIL
A stronger magnet has a larger magnetic field B
Since F ∝ B, a larger B produces a greater force, which results in a larger displacement
rubric.expected_answer: The force on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field is given by F = BIL, where B is the magnetic field strength. A stronger magnet produces a larger value of B. Since force is directly proportional to B (F ∝ B), a stronger magnet exerts a greater force on the conductor, causing a larger displacement.

questions.text: State THREE precautions that should be taken to avoid overloading in domestic electric circuits.

keywords: do not connect too many appliances
key_points: 1. Do not connect too many high-power appliances to a single socket or circuit simultaneously
2. Use separate circuits for high-power appliances (e.g., AC, geyser, oven) rather than a single shared circuit
3. Always use the correct fuse/MCB with an appropriate current rating for each circuit
rubric.expected_answer: (1) Do not plug too many appliances into a single socket/circuit at the same time. (2) Use separate circuits with appropriate ratings for high-power appliances. (3) Always fit the correct rated fuse or MCB — do not replace a blown fuse with one of higher rating.

questions.text: Using the Right-Hand Thumb Rule, determine the direction of the magnetic field at a point to the east of a vertical wire in which current flows upward. Explain your reasoning step by step.

key_points: Thumb points upward (current direction)
Fingers curl around the wire: on the east side, fingers point towards south
Therefore the magnetic field at a point to the east of the wire is directed towards south
rubric.expected_answer: Step 1: Hold the wire in the right hand with thumb pointing upward (direction of current). Step 2: The curled fingers wrap around the wire — on the east side of the wire, the fingers point towards the south direction. Step 3: Therefore, the magnetic field at a point to the east of the wire is directed towards south (from east looking at wire, field goes southward).

questions.text: A student claims: 'Magnetic field lines are open curves — they start from the north pole and end at the south pole.' Is this claim correct? Justify your answer with the complete behaviour of field lines.

key_points: The claim is PARTIALLY correct but incomplete and therefore incorrect
Outside the magnet: field lines go from N-pole to S-pole — this part is correct
Inside the magnet: field lines continue from S-pole back to N-pole
Therefore field lines form complete CLOSED LOOPS; they do not start or end anywhere
rubric.expected_answer: The claim is incorrect. While it is true that outside the magnet the field lines appear to go from N to S, inside the magnet they continue from S back to N, forming complete closed loops. Magnetic field lines have no beginning and no end — they are continuous closed curves. Unlike electric field lines (which start on positive and end on negative charges), magnetic field lines have no isolated poles where they terminate.

questions.text: An electric appliance of power P watts is connected to a supply of V volts. Calculate the current drawn by the appliance.

key_points: I = P / V
rubric.expected_answer: Current I = P / V amperes

questions.text: A circular coil has n turns. The magnetic field at its centre due to a single turn carrying current I is B₀. Find the total magnetic field at the centre of the n-turn coil.

key_points: Total field = n × B₀
rubric.expected_answer: B = n × B₀

questions.text: An appliance of power P watts is connected to V volts. A fuse of rating I_f amperes is installed. Calculate whether the fuse will blow under normal operating conditions.

key_points: Calculate operating current: I = P / V
If I > I_f, the fuse will blow
If I ≤ I_f, the fuse will not blow
rubric.expected_answer: I = P/V. If I > I_f: fuse blows. If I ≤ I_f: fuse does not blow.

questions.text:
An electric motor in a mixer grinder is protected by a 5 A circuit breaker. The motor spins in reverse when the battery terminals are swapped.

(a) State the principle on which an electric motor works. [1]
(b) Name the rule that determines the direction of motion of the motor coil. [1]
(c) State two ways to increase the rotational speed of the motor. [2]

key_points: Motor works on: current-carrying conductor in magnetic field experiences mechanical force
Fleming's Left Hand Rule gives direction of force/motion
Increase speed: increase current OR increase magnetic field strength OR increase number of coil turns
Commutator reverses current direction every half turn to maintain continuous rotation
rubric.expected_answer: (a) A current-carrying conductor placed in a magnetic field experiences a force. (b) Fleming's Left Hand Rule. (c) Increase current; increase strength of magnetic field (use stronger magnets); increase number of turns in the armature coil.

questions.text: According to Fleming's Left Hand Rule, which finger points in the direction of the magnetic field?

key_points: In Fleming's Left Hand Rule: Index finger = direction of magnetic field (B), Middle finger = direction of conventional current (I), Thumb = direction of force/motion on conductor (F).
Memory aid: FBI — Forefinger = B (field), Centre/middle = I (current), thuMb = Motion.
rubric.expected_answer: Option B — Index finger (forefinger) points in the direction of the magnetic field.

questions.text: A current-carrying conductor is placed in a magnetic field. The force on the conductor will be maximum when the angle between the conductor and the magnetic field is:

key_points: Force F = BIL sin(theta), where theta is the angle between the conductor and magnetic field.
sin(90 degrees) = 1 is the maximum value, so force is maximum when conductor is perpendicular to the field.
When theta = 0 or 180 degrees (conductor parallel to field), sin = 0, so F = 0.
rubric.expected_answer: Option C — 90 degrees. Force is maximum when conductor is perpendicular to the magnetic field.

questions.text: Fleming's Left Hand Rule is used to find the direction of force on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field. This rule applies to which device?

key_points: Fleming's Left Hand Rule gives the direction of mechanical force on a current-carrying conductor — this is the principle of an electric motor (electrical energy to mechanical energy).
Fleming's Right Hand Rule applies to generators (mechanical energy to electrical energy).
Left Hand = motor (Left Hand = L = Lorentz force on current).
rubric.expected_answer: Option C — Electric motor. The left-hand rule predicts the force that drives rotation in a motor.

questions.text: State the factors that affect the magnitude of the force on a current-carrying conductor placed in a magnetic field.

key_points: Factor 1: Strength of the magnetic field (B) — greater field, greater force.
Factor 2: Magnitude of the current (I) — greater current, greater force.
Factor 3: Length of the conductor in the field (L) — longer conductor, greater force.
Factor 4: Angle between conductor and field (theta) — F = BIL sin(theta); maximum at 90 degrees, zero when parallel.
Combining: F = BIL sin(theta)
rubric.expected_answer: Force depends on: (i) magnetic field strength B, (ii) current I, (iii) length of conductor L, (iv) angle between conductor and field. F = BIL sin(theta).

questions.text: Explain how the direction of force on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field reverses when (i) the direction of current is reversed, and (ii) the direction of the magnetic field is reversed.

key_points: By Fleming's Left Hand Rule, force direction depends on both the current direction and the field direction.
(i) Reversing current: middle finger (current) points in opposite direction => thumb (force) reverses direction.
(ii) Reversing magnetic field: index finger (field) points opposite => thumb (force) reverses direction.
Reversing both current AND field simultaneously: force direction stays the same (two reversals cancel out).
This principle is why a DC motor's rotation reverses when supply terminals are swapped.
rubric.expected_answer: Reversing current reverses the force direction. Reversing the magnetic field also reverses the force direction. Reversing both keeps force direction unchanged.
